alerts.headline: Flood Warning issued October 22 at 7:28PM MDT until October 22 at 10:00PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Small stream flooding caused by excessive rainfall
continues.

* WHERE...Western Conejos County in south central Colorado...
Southwestern Rio Grande County in south central Colorado...

* WHEN...Until 1000 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 725 PM MDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
heavy rain. Flooding is already occurring in the warned area.
Between 1 and 3 inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are possible in the
warned area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Conejos River, La Jara Creek, Alamosa Creek and their
tributaries.
- Saturated ground will lead to continuous runoff from additional
rainfall overnight. Climb to higher ground if flood waters
threaten.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

alerts.headline: Flood Warning issued October 22 at 6:49PM MDT until October 25 at 6:00PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
alerts.description:
...The National Weather Service in Pueblo has issued a Flood Warning
for the following rivers in Colorado...

Rio Grande Near Del Norte affecting Rio Grande County.

For the Upper Rio Grande River...including Del Norte...Minor flooding
is forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Rio Grande  near Del Norte.

* WHEN...From Friday morning to Sunday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 6.0 feet, Minor Flood. Considerable agricultural
flooding occurs.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 5:45 PM MDT Thursday the stage was 4.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 5.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage
tomorrow morning to a crest of 6.0 feet tomorrow evening. It will
then fall below flood stage Sunday morning.
- Flood stage is 5.5 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 5.9
feet on 06/09/1985.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

alerts.headline: Flood Warning issued October 22 at 6:41PM MDT until October 23 at 3:45AM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Small stream flooding caused by excessive rainfall is
expected.

* WHERE...Southern Mineral County in south central Colorado...
Western Rio Grande County in south central Colorado...

* WHEN...Until 345 AM MDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Rock falls are
occuring in the steeper terrain.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 639 PM MDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
heavy rain. Flooding is already occurring in the warned area.
Between 1 and 3.5 inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts up to 2 inches are possible in the
warned area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Wolf Creek Pass and the creeks and streams flowing into the San
Juan River.
- Highway 160 over Wolf Creek Pass is closed due to flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

alerts.headline: Flood Warning issued October 22 at 5:59PM MDT until October 22 at 10:15PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
alerts.description:
Heavy rainfall is causing flooding along the South Fork of the Rio
Grande, which is forecast to crest at 9.2 feet around 1 AM tonight.
If you live near the South Fork of the Rio Grande, and the main stem
of the Rio Grande, take precautions to protect life and property from
flooding.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Southwestern Saguache, Central Mineral and Western Rio
Grande Counties...

* WHEN...Until 1015 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Several
structures are flooded and some sand bagging operations are
continuing. Streams continue to rise due to excess runoff from
continued rainfall.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 552 PM MDT, South Fork Fire and Colorado State Patrol report
continued rainfall across the warned area.
- Water is currently near Highway 160 at Wolf Creek Ranch at mile
marker 177.  Several homes are also being flooded in the South
Fork area.  The river gauge on the south fork of the Rio Grande
(SRGC2) is rapidly rising, and forecast to crest at 9.2 feet by 1
AM tonight, and slowly fall during the overnight hours.  The main
stem of the Rio Grande will likely run high down toward Del
Norte.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Del Norte, South Fork, Wagon Wheel Gap, Wolf Creek Pass and
Creede.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

alerts.description:

possible.

* WHERE...The eastern San Juan Mountains and Upper Rio Grande Valley.

* WHEN...Through Friday afternoon.

creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

heavy rain across the area from tonight into Friday morning
before winding down Friday afternoon.
- The eastern San Juan Mountains and Upper Rio Grande Valley.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

alerts.title: US 160 Pagosa Springs Reconstruction-147600
alerts.description: Between US 84 and Pike Drive (Pagosa Springs) from Mile Point 144.3 to Mile Point 141.8. Road construction. Starting October 24, 2026 at 7:00AM MDT until October 24, 2026 at about 6:00PM MDT. Full schedule below: • October 24, 7:00AM - October 24, 6:00PM Comment: Harman Park & Piedra Road-Work is underway at this intersection of US 160. Working hours will be intermittent day and night so motorists should plan for potential delays, Monday-Saturday. Please allow extra time to get through the work zone. Safety benefits of this work includes pedestrian safety upgrades and ADA accessibility improvements. Expect lane shifts and up to 15-minute delays. Crews will switch two-way traffic into the eastbound lanes, perform temporary striping operations and begin asphalt milling in the westbound lanes. Parking will not be permitted on US 160 and vehicles will be towed at the owner's expense. Westbound lane closures, 10’ width and 75’ length restrictions will remain in place 24/7 through end of 2026. Work is weather-dependent. For questions contact the project team at 970-335-9230 or Pagosa160reconstruction@gmail.com Project Webpage: www.codot.gov/projects/us160pagosasprings
